clue.text: Taking fruit to fill up, figure should be trim

indicators.note: the fruit is put inside so as to fill the figure up

parts.note: a figure is a shape or outline
hips are the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: A dieter told to eat fruit to keep their figure slim.
explanation.definitionFit: Something neat and in good order is said to be trim, like a well-kept vessel.

clue.text: A German woman's partner?

parts.note: read as a woman's partner, the man belonging to her, which also happens to be a German given name

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase splits as a pronoun plus a husband, and the whole is a common German forename.

clue.text: A step to view as outdated

parts.note: pas is a dance step, from French
to see is to view

explanation.surface: Someone stepping back to judge something old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Passee is the feminine of a French word for past, used of things no longer in fashion.

clue.text: He would swallow freshly-made tea very hot

indicators.note: the contracted pronoun-and-verb takes the rearranged drink down inside it

parts.note: contracted to he'd, written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: a fresh brew remakes the letters of the drink in a new order

explanation.surface: A man gulping down a newly brewed cup of scalding tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He would' contracts to he'd, written without its apostrophe; 'freshly-made' signals the anagram of the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heated has been warmed until it is very hot.

clue.text: Coppers stay to take control

parts.note: copper coins are pence, abbreviated P
to reside is to stay or live somewhere

explanation.surface: Police officers remaining at a scene to take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police but here means copper coins: P for penny or pence.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to chair or be in charge of a meeting.

clue.text: The fool will go easy on the heavyweight

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: simple means easy
a ton is a heavy unit of weight

explanation.surface: Advice that only a fool would go gently against a heavyweight boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish, gullible person.

clue.text: Called for housing once in vain

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it like a house

parts.note: cited can mean summoned or called for
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone once demanded accommodation in vain.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceited person is proud of themselves, full of vanity.

clue.text: Get through to bore

definitions.meaning: to pass right into or through something

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean making a way into or through something, as a drill does.

clue.text: The medico in revolt cracked

indicators.note: the doctor is placed inside the uprising

parts.note: a rise or rising is a revolt
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A doctor caught up in an uprising has gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' suggests crazy but is the botanical sense of a surface full of cracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimose is a botanical term for a surface covered in fissures, like bark.

clue.text: Shellfish cure a cat's disorder

indicators.note: the letters are put into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: the S is used as a letter here

explanation.surface: A remedy for a cat's illness made from seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Crustacea is the class of hard-shelled creatures such as crabs and lobsters.

clue.text: Brave article on quiet suffering

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
p is piano, musical notation for quiet
an ache is pain or suffering

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about someone silently in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' as a noun is a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: An Apache warrior is a brave, the old term for a Native American fighter.

clue.text: Notes framed by a clergyman, laid carelessly out by a reckless person

indicators.note: the scrambled word sits outside, around the rest
laid down carelessly, the letters are jumbled
the notes sit inside the clergyman like a picture in a frame

parts.note: Rev is the abbreviation for reverend
D and E are musical notes

explanation.surface: Notes left by a vicar, scattered about by some rash person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framed by' and 'carelessly' each work on their own piece, and 'out' wraps the jumbled word around the framed notes; 'by a reckless person' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is someone who takes bold, rash risks.

clue.text: The elder rose in confusion

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into confusion and reordered

explanation.surface: An older person's rose bush in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like a verb or flower; both it and 'in' are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior is an older person, the elder of two.

clue.text: Fish that's a food for cows in a Hebridean isle

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the island name

parts.note: Barra is an island in the Outer Hebrides off Scotland
cud is food chewed again by cattle

explanation.surface: A fish described as cattle fodder on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: A barracuda is a large predatory sea fish with sharp teeth.

clue.text: Every one included in the list may be given instruction

indicators.note: the first piece is placed within the second

parts.note: a table is a list or chart
each means every one

explanation.surface: Anyone on the list is fit to receive lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone teachable is able to learn, open to being taught.

clue.text: Cuts race least well-organised

indicators.note: the letters are organised into a new order

explanation.surface: A badly arranged race being cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or gash the flesh, making cuts.

clue.text: Some adorable animals may be seen in this field

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Cute animals grazing in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a meadow or grassy field, a poetic word.

clue.text: The sovereign a top newsman guided

parts.note: a sovereign is a gold pound coin, and L is the pound sign's abbreviation
ed is short for editor, the chief at a newspaper

explanation.surface: A monarch and a leading journalist showed the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' suggests a monarch; here it is the coin worth a pound, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Led is the past tense of lead, to guide or direct.

clue.text: A left-half will get the beer

parts.note: taken as written; the run of letters across these printed words matching the solution is coincidence

indicators.note: only half of the word, its opening two letters, is used

explanation.surface: A footballer in the left-half position earns a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A left-half was a midfield position in old football formations; here 'half' takes half of 'left'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is a type of beer.

clue.text: Having to state one's date of birth is normal

parts.note: to aver is to declare or state
age is reckoned from one's date of birth

explanation.surface: Being asked your birth date is routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means ordinary or typical, what is usual.

clue.text: Sets out after game that's totally unrestrained

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the game

parts.note: loo is an old card game

indicators.note: the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Sets lost after a wild match.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosest is the superlative of loose, meaning most free or unrestrained.

clue.text: The right of the French egghead

parts.note: du is French for of the
read as the head of an egg, its first letter

explanation.surface: An intellectual's rights in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but splits into head of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: One's due is what one is owed, one's entitlement.

clue.text: Good but not grand

definitions.meaning: a piano that is not a grand is the vertical kind

explanation.definitionFit: Upright means virtuous, and an upright piano is the vertical alternative to a grand.

clue.text: A signal of distress found in the herb garden

definitions.meaning: a flare fired into the sky to call for help
a salad leaf with a peppery taste, also called arugula

explanation.definitionFit: A distress flare is a firework-like projectile, and the same name is given to the peppery salad herb arugula.

clue.text: Back a relentless union

parts.note: stern can mean harsh and unyielding

explanation.surface: Supporting a hard-line trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a verb meaning support; it is the sailing direction toward the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means at or toward the back of a ship.

clue.text: Setting many on edge with each area of conflict

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A tense situation that puts many people on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean peninsula has been fought over repeatedly, from the 1850s war onwards.

clue.text: Doesn't get befuddled when intoxicated

indicators.note: the letters become confused and so are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who stays clear-headed even when drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoned is slang for drunk or high on drugs.

clue.text: Fear trust management check

indicators.note: managing the letters means organising them into another order

explanation.surface: Fear and trust in managers being kept in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To frustrate a plan is to thwart or check it.

clue.text: A knotty problem for the dandy?

definitions.text: A knotty problem for the dandy?

parts.words: A knotty problem for the dandy?
parts.note: a fashionable man's neckwear that must be tied in a knot

explanation.definitionFit: A dandy wears a neckcloth tied around the throat, so his problem is literally knotted.

clue.text: Bond, given a welcome, set about the guys!

indicators.note: the welcome is placed around the guys

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
men means guys

explanation.surface: James Bond, warmly received, attacking the villains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests the spy; it means a pact or contract. 'set about' also looks like 'attack'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is a binding contract or pact between parties.

clue.text: Flat-quarters for one-time us statesman

parts.note: dull means flat or lifeless
E and S are compass points, or quarters

explanation.surface: Lodgings in an apartment for a former American politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat-quarters' suggests apartment lodgings; it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: John Foster Dulles was US Secretary of State under Eisenhower.

clue.text: Colours models

definitions.meaning: flags or banners, as carried by a regiment

explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's flags are its standards, and a standard is also a benchmark of quality.
